uncited: *   **4D-Cell:** A $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ neighborhood of toxels.
*   **Vector Path Table (Table 2):** A lookup table with 32 rows (Center IDs 0–31) and 18 columns.
Columns are grouped by orientation ($\oplus$ or $\ominus$) and path index (1, 2, 3).
*   **Boundary Volume Octant (BVO):** Each of the 16 toxels contributes 4 BVOs based on the orientation of the range vector (positive/negative $x, y, z, t$).
**Segment Data:** Compare each toxel's field value to the iso-value.
**Identify Transitions:** For each $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ 4D-cell, identify active-to-inactive transitions.
**Lookup Vector Paths:** Use the Vector Path Table (Table 2) to determine the 192 possible TCV pairs within the 4D-cell.
**Generate Protomesh:** Concatenate the TCVs to form initial cyclic vector paths.
*   *Triangular Strut:* If two BVOs have opposite orientations (e.g., $18\oplus$ and $18\ominus$), their TCVs cancel, resulting in no contribution.
**Resolve Ambiguities:** If a juncture is a Point of Ambiguity (POA) (paths start/end at the same juncture, e.g., juncture 47), use the connectivity diagram to resolve connections.
*   *Mixed Mode:* Assign the average field value of toxels at positions I, II, III, IV to the POA.
**Discard Junctures:** Remove all junctures (point IDs > 31) from the protomesh.
This reduces cyclic paths to final tetrahedrons.
Mark the center of mass point (face center) for each 4-cycle.
Decompose surface cycles into triangles by connecting face centers with corresponding 4-cycle support points.
Collect triangles enclosing a volume, determine the absolute center of the enclosed volume.
Connect face centers with the absolute volume center.
*   *LR Decomposition:* Replace steps of marking face centers and connecting them with N-cycle decompositions without additional center of mass points.
Omit the step connecting face centers to volume center.
**Repeat for Isolated Toxels:** For a single isolated active toxel, process the remaining 15 4D-cells to generate a total of 16 oriented tetrahedrons.
It processes each $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ 4D-cell independently, similar to VESTA.

*   **When not to use:** When 3D data is sufficient (use VESTA).
When computational resources are extremely limited and approximate results are acceptable.
